title: Engineer growth 1:1 cheat sheet — Quentin + Maya
content:
Context: Maya -> IC3 backend engineer (serving-runtime team). Been at Redwood ~14 months. Running the LRU cache refactor spike; interested in IC4 roadmap and mentoring opportunities. Last 1:1 we talked about prioritization and pairing on the KV cache perf regression (INF-4821).

Meeting logistics (30m):
- 0-5m: personal check-in (mood, anything urgent)
- 5-15m: status update on KV cache refactor + blockers (quick demo if useful)
- 15-23m: growth focus (career thread, IC4 expectations, mentorship options)
- 23-27m: decisions & prioritization (do we pause tech debt? ship canary?)
- 27-30m: action items + quick feedback

Top goals to align on this quarter (reminder lines):
- Ship LRU cache refactor with <10% regression target (metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory usage)
- Lead at least one cross-team postmortem and run the blameless write-up
- Start mentoring rotation: 1x rotation pair/week for 6 weeks

Signals to probe (questions to ask):
- "What progress did you unblock since last time? Any surprises?"
- "How confident are you in the perf numbers? show me the benchmark command you ran"
- "Do you want to own the rollout plan for the canary or prefer I take the ops steps?"
- "Any dev morale/overwork signals I should know about?"

Current status notes (what Maya said in sync + my quick take):
- Local perf numbers look good (5–8% median improvement) but p95 spikes on long sequences (repro steps in PR notes).
- She flagged flaky integration test on a small subset of models (INF-4821). Suspect race in KV warmup path.
- She expressed interest in mentoring and asked about roadmap promotion timing — believes shes production-ready for IC4 stretch projects.

Blockers / Risks to escalate:
- Flaky test is blocking canary. If we push without fix, rollback risk increases. Escalation: ask SRE on duty to look at infra trace window (ticket INF-4821).
- Lack of dedicated perf runs in CI—need to request quota for nightly GPU runs. Action: I'll open JIRA infra request and cc Maya.

Hypothesis to test (short experiment plan):
- Hypothesis: race occurs when KV warmup and concurrent streaming start within 200ms of each other.
- Quick experiment: add a configurable warmup delay in staging, run 50 long-seq streams concurrently, compare failure rate. (owner: Maya, ETA: 3 days)

Mentorship / growth items to cover:
- Concrete IC4 stretch projects: own cross-region fallback routing + lead the rollout (high visibility).
- Coaching on running a postmortem: suggested checklist and run-through (I will pair as co-author first time).
- Feedback practice: have Maya prepare a 90s "what I learned" after each pairing session to practice concise updates.

Notes for feedback to give (gentle, actionable):
- Positive: strong ownership on the refactor, clear instrumentation. Call out the good commit messages and test vectors.
- Improvement: scope signals—don't try to optimize the whole pipeline in one PR; split out deterministic changes vs perf heuristics.

Decisions needed in this meeting (I should make or confirm):
- Pause surface-level optimizations that touch runtime until flaky test root cause is identified? My leaning: pause, isolate, fix.
- Who runs the canary? Proposal: Maya owns code; I coordinate ops rollout. Confirm now.

Action items (post-meeting draft email snippet for Maya):
- "Thanks for today's sync — agreed actions: (1) run warmup-delay experiment in staging (owner: Maya, ETA: 2026-05-31), (2) I'll open infra JIRA to request nightly GPU quota (owner: Quentin), (3) pair on postmortem doc next Thursday. I'll also ping SRE about INF-4821. I'll follow up with links + checklist."

Quick todo for me before the 1:1:
- skim PR #998 and summarize known regressions (10–15m)
- open infra JIRA for nightly perf runs (INF-XXXX placeholder)
- prepare one example sentence of career ladder evidence for IC4 (concrete example)

Loose notes / things to remember (notes-to-self style):
- Maya values autonomy; give runway and clear escalation path.
- Offer to introduce to Priya (pm) to scope IC4 cross-team work.
- Remember to celebrate small wins: call out the bench perf improvement in public Slack.

Follow-ups to capture in Jira/Confluence after meeting:
- Update CONFLUENCE:CON-7721-career-framework with Maya's evidence paragraph for promotion packet.
- Link experiment results to INF-4821.

Open questions to track in next meeting:
- Did the warmup-delay experiment reduce failure rate? pick numbers.
- Any upstream model changes affecting p95?
- Mentor pairing: is weekly 1hr sustainable? adjust cadence.

Draft closing line for the 1:1: "Appreciate the focus on instrumentation + tests — let's get the flaky integration test stable this week so your canary goes smoothly."

Raw scratch lines (copy-pasteable into Slack or email):
- "Maya — quick follow-up: can you paste the exact benchmark command you ran and the p95 numbers? I'm collating numbers for the canary plan."
- "Will open infra ticket for nightly GPU perf runs and tag you. If we get that CI, we can catch regressions early."

-- end of notes --
